A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same CRAFT framework and τ-break benchmark. Their text, equations, tables, figures and complete appendices support reliable comparison, including matching relocated and renamed material.

before.justification: v1 reports original attack-success measurements, component ablations and defense evaluations on airline and retail tasks, with additional results in Appendices D and H.

after.justification: v3 retains these original experiments and adds an 8B-attacker evaluation and a manual analysis of the benchmark's violation types in Appendix I.

M1.justification: CRAFT's four components, attack prompts, benchmark-construction procedure and three defense methods remain unchanged. Expanded explanations and newly documented reuse of planning outputs do not establish a procedural change.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same 20 airline and 30 retail cases derived from τ-bench. The smaller-attacker experiment reuses these domains, and the new violation taxonomy characterizes existing cases rather than adding coverage.

E2.justification: The evaluated comparators remain the τ-bench user simulator, DAN, emotional manipulation, direct prompt injection and insistent prompting. 'Cooperative,' 'non-strategic' and 'naïve' refer to the same simulator baseline. The new 8B experiment also compares CRAFT with that existing baseline.

E3.justification: Appendix I adds LLaMA-3.1-8B-Instruct as an attacker configuration, retaining four repetitions and pass@k evaluation. The established experiments retain their settings. The new experiment does not explicitly identify its target model, limiting comparisons with the earlier model configurations.

E4.justification: v3 adds a limited attacker-capacity analysis using an 8B model and manually categorizes all 50 benchmark cases into four violation types. Existing component ablations, defense analyses and example trajectories remain unchanged.

E5.justification: Both versions report four trials per task and the same pass@k estimator. Seed 10 moves from v1 Appendix C.1 to v3 Section 5.2. The added experiment follows the existing reporting practice; neither version provides confidence intervals, variance estimates or significance tests.

E6.justification: Table 1 corrects GPT-4o self-attack entries in the 'as agent' blocks: airline pass@1 baseline/CRAFT changes from 37.5/42.5 to 42.5/70.0, and retail CRAFT changes from 0.0 to 2.5, with corresponding higher-k corrections. These match results already reported elsewhere. New Table 7 reports 8B-attacker baseline/CRAFT pass@1 values of 28.8/47.5 for airline and 1.3/2.5 for retail. Table 8 adds violation-category proportions of 48%, 28%, 12% and 12%.

T1.justification: New Appendix I defines a call-count model using requests n, repetitions r and dialogue turns t, deriving O(nrt + 3n) = O(nrt) + O(n) under once-per-task planning reuse. v1 lacks this complexity argument. Existing set-difference and pass@k mathematics remain unchanged.

C1.justification: The abstract and central contributions retain the same scope: policy-aware CRAFT attacks, the τ-break security benchmark, stronger attacks than generic baselines and insufficient lightweight defenses. The rewritten conclusion restates these claims without materially changing them.

C2.justification: v3 interprets the new analyses as supporting modest planning overhead and feasibility with smaller attackers. Section 10 newly explains the engineering burden of extending τ-break to other domains and removes the five-model limitation paragraph. Existing failure-mechanism and defense interpretations remain substantially unchanged.

D1.justification: v3 names IBM/CRAFT as the destination for a future code/data release and specifies reuse of all three planning outputs across repetitions. The 30-turn limit and seed information relocate to Section 5.2, but v1's explicit temperature=0 setting disappears. These are documentation changes, not evidence of a changed temperature or completed release.

R1.justification: v3 adds Jin et al. (2024), relating deceptive contextual framing to prior induction attacks, plus citations to GPT-4o, Llama 3, DeepSeek-V3 and Qwen3 reports. The broader positioning relative to τ-bench and generic red-teaming remains unchanged.

P1.justification: v3 expands the explanation of benchmark conversion, clarifies and renames the simulator baseline, converts failure motifs into explanatory bullets, and rewrites the conclusion and limitations. Experimental setup details move into the main text. These are localized revisions within the retained overall structure.

P2.justification: v3 redisplays the existing Appendix A attack trajectory on the first page as Figure 1, adds Tables 7–8, and updates baseline labels in figures and tables. Existing diagrams, plots and table structures are largely retained; the first-page trajectory is not a new case study.

improvement.justification: v3 improves clarity and internal consistency through a clearer baseline description and corrections to Table 1. The smaller-attacker experiment and violation-type breakdown provide useful, limited evidence about feasibility and benchmark composition. These gains are tempered by removal of the explicit temperature setting and the new experiment's unspecified target model, so the improvement is modest.
